description: Personal email assistant with mailbox search, thread retrieval, and unread-summary tools.

tools.name: search_email
tools.description: Search the user's mailbox. Returns messages whose received timestamp falls in [received_after, received_before). Both bounds are required and must be UTC ISO 8601 strings (e.g. 2026-07-01T04:00:00Z); received_after is inclusive, received_before is exclusive.

params.name: query
params.description: Free-text subject/body filter (optional; empty matches all messages in range)

tools.name: get_latest_thread
tools.description: Return the most recent email thread matching the query, with every message in the thread (sender and received timestamp). No time filtering.

params.name: query
params.description: Free-text filter over thread subject and participants

tools.name: get_unread_summary
tools.description: Return the user's currently unread messages (sender, subject, received timestamp), newest first. No parameters, no time filtering.

scenarios.title: dana-earlier-this-week
scenarios.user: How many emails did Dana send me earlier this week?

verifyPhrase.disagreementNote: nl2time ends 'earlier this week' at 2026-07-15T04:00Z — the start of YESTERDAY (Wed Jul 15 00:00 ET) — excluding all of Wednesday even though now is Thursday, so its window ends before the core (which runs to Wed 4pm ET). The benchmark admits week-start (Sun or Mon convention) through start-of-today / now / end-of-today / end-of-week; excluding Wednesday from 'earlier this week' on a Thursday is an nl2time quirk to report

checks.note: Dana's Tue Jul 14 and Wed Jul 15 messages; her Jul 9 email is last week and the Wed newsletter is a different sender

scenarios.rationale: Now = THURSDAY Jul 16 2026, 9:30am EDT (UTC-4) — midweek so Sunday-start and Monday-start weeks agree on the interior. Window grading (core/envelope per the 2026-07-26 blind-audit adjudication): CORE = minimal round-local-hour interval containing all three intended in-range rows (Dana Tue Jul 14 10:05am, newsletter Wed Jul 15 12:10pm, Dana Wed Jul 15 3:40pm EDT) = [Tue 10:00 ET, Wed 16:00 ET) = [2026-07-14T14:00Z, 2026-07-15T20:00Z). ENVELOPE = the 'earlier this week' policy family [locale-or-ISO week start, end-of-week]: earliest defensible start = Sun Jul 12 00:00 ET (en-US CLDR week start) = 2026-07-12T04:00Z; latest defensible end = Mon-start week end Mon Jul 20 00:00 ET = 2026-07-20T04:00Z (rows never postdate now, so end-of-week readings agree with end=now/start-of-today/end-of-today readings). Answer-invariant: core and envelope both select the same 3 rows — Dana Jul 9 (Thu last week, 09T15:00Z) precedes the envelope start, and no rows lie after Wed 3:40pm within the envelope. Dana's count is 2 under every reading (the newsletter is the wrong sender).

scenarios.title: anything-over-the-weekend
scenarios.user: Did anything come in over the weekend? Tell me the day each one arrived.

checks.note: Saturday photos + Sunday-night reunion email; Friday delivery and Monday standup are outside the weekend
Photos arrived Saturday July 18 (5:15pm EDT; UTC day agrees)
Reunion email arrived Sunday July 19, 11:10pm EDT — the UTC timestamp reads Monday July 20 and must not be given as the day

scenarios.rationale: Now = MONDAY Jul 20 2026, 6:40pm EDT (UTC-4), so 'over the weekend' is unambiguously the just-ended Sat–Sun: Sat Jul 18 00:00 ET .. Mon Jul 20 00:00 ET = [2026-07-18T04:00Z, 2026-07-20T04:00Z) — nl2time agrees. Trap: the Aunt Carol row 2026-07-20T03:10Z is Sunday Jul 19 11:10pm EDT — inside the local weekend but excluded by naive UTC-day bounds [18T00Z, 20T00Z), and its UTC day (Monday Jul 20) is the wrong answer day. The Luis row 2026-07-18T21:15Z = Saturday 5:15pm EDT (UTC and local day agree — plain civilDay). FreshDirect (Fri 4:30pm EDT) and Greg (Mon 9:05am EDT) are outside. Count = 2.

scenarios.title: landlord-count-in-june
scenarios.user: How many emails did my landlord send me in June?

checks.note: Jun 10, Jun 24, and the Jun 30 10:15pm rent reminder; the May-31-11pm receipt is not June

scenarios.rationale: Now = Tuesday Jul 14 2026, 8:20am EDT. June as a civil month in New York (EDT, UTC-4 throughout): Jun 1 00:00 ET .. Jul 1 00:00 ET = [2026-06-01T04:00Z, 2026-07-01T04:00Z) — nl2time agrees. Symmetric UTC trap at both boundaries: the 'Rent receipt' row 2026-06-01T03:00Z is Sunday MAY 31 11:00pm EDT — outside local June but inside a naive UTC June window — while the 'Rent reminder' row 2026-07-01T02:15Z is Tuesday JUNE 30 10:15pm EDT — inside local June but outside naive UTC June. Correct landlord count = 3 (Jun 10, Jun 24, Jun 30); naive UTC bounds also give 3 but the wrong set — the count stays a valid discriminator only jointly with the graded bounds. The bank row (Jun 18) is in range but the wrong sender.

scenarios.title: past-48-hours
scenarios.user: How many messages have come in over the past 48 hours?

checks.note: Jul 30 11:30am, Jul 31 6:10pm, Aug 1 9:00am ET; the 10:05-Thursday draft-contract email is 49h05m old

scenarios.rationale: Now = SATURDAY Aug 1 2026, 10:05am EDT (UTC-4) = 2026-08-01T14:05Z — deliberately just past a month boundary. 'The past 48 hours' is hour-grain arithmetic from now, not a civil-day window: [now - 48h, now] = [2026-07-30T14:05Z, 2026-08-01T14:05Z) — nl2time agrees exactly. In range: Contract signed (30T15:30Z, 47h25m ago), GitHub (31T22:10Z), Sam (01T13:00Z) = 3. The Draft-contract row 30T13:00Z is 49h05m old — 65 minutes before the start — and punishes rounding to whole civil days ([Jul 30 00:00 ET, now] would count 4). No UTC/local day trickery; the trap is purely the hour-grain start bound.

scenarios.title: priya-reply-when
scenarios.user: When exactly did Priya reply to my note about the lease renewal?

messages.name: Andy Brook
messages.body_preview: Priya - can you look over the renewal terms?

messages.name: Priya Nair

checks.note: Reply landed Friday July 17, 11:22pm EDT; the UTC timestamp reads July 18 and must not be given as the day
If a clock time is given it must be 11:22 pm local, not 3:22

scenarios.rationale: Pure time->NL: get_latest_thread takes no time params and returns Priya's reply timestamped 2026-07-18T03:22Z. In America/New_York (EDT, UTC-4) that is FRIDAY JULY 17, 11:22pm. Correct answers say July 17 (and 11:22 pm if a time is given); 'July 18' and '3:22' are the naive UTC readings and fail. search_email is also mocked consistently (the reply row plus the landlord's original paperwork email two days earlier) so a model that searches instead of pulling the thread sees the same timestamp.

scenarios.title: kolkata-three-days-ago
scenarios.user: How many emails came in 3 days ago? And when did the first one arrive?

checks.note: Build-failure (1:30am IST) and design-review (2:45pm IST) on Tue Aug 4; 'Build fixed' is 00:40 IST Aug 5
First arrival is 1:30 am IST, not the UTC clock reading 8:00 pm

scenarios.rationale: Now = FRIDAY Aug 7 2026, 11:45am IST (Asia/Kolkata, non-integer offset +05:30). '3 days ago' = the civil day Tuesday Aug 4 in Kolkata: [Aug 4 00:00 IST, Aug 5 00:00 IST) = [2026-08-03T18:30Z, 2026-08-04T18:30Z) — bounds land at :30 past the UTC hour; nl2time agrees exactly. Traps: the build-failure row 2026-08-03T20:00Z is Tue Aug 4 1:30am IST — inside, though its UTC day is Aug 3 — while 'Build fixed' 2026-08-04T19:10Z is Wed Aug 5 12:40am IST — outside, though its UTC day is Aug 4. Naive UTC-day bounds [04T00Z, 05T00Z) select exactly the wrong pair. Count = 2; the first arrival renders as 1:30 am IST (UTC clock 8:00 pm rejected). The Zomato row (Sun Aug 2) is well outside.

scenarios.title: legal-week-of-the-6th
scenarios.user: How many emails did Legal send me the week of the 6th?

checks.note: NDA (Tue Jul 7) + redlines (Thu Jul 9); the MSA email is the following week and the badge audit is not from Legal

scenarios.rationale: Now = Wednesday Jul 22 2026, 9:00am EDT. July 6 2026 is a MONDAY; 'the week of the 6th' is the week containing it: Sunday-start (en-US CLDR) Sun Jul 5 .. Sun Jul 12 = [2026-07-05T04:00Z, 2026-07-12T04:00Z), or Monday-start (ISO) Mon Jul 6 .. Mon Jul 13 = [2026-07-06T04:00Z, 2026-07-13T04:00Z). nl2time returns the Sunday-start tuple. Disputed edge days are Sun Jul 5 (only in the Sun-start reading) and Sun Jul 12 (only in the Mon-start reading) — no rows on either, so both tuples select the same 3 rows (Legal Jul 7, Legal Jul 9, Facilities Jul 8). Legal count = 2; the Jul 15 MSA email is outside both readings and the Facilities row is the wrong sender.

scenarios.title: newest-unread-arrival
scenarios.user: I've been off the grid for a couple of days. When did the most recent unread email in my inbox arrive?

checks.note: Newest unread (IT Helpdesk) arrived July 23; UTC and local day agree — trap-free baseline
July 23 2026 is a Thursday in New York

scenarios.rationale: Pure time->NL, deliberately trap-free (honest baseline). Now = Saturday Jul 25 2026, 10:00am EDT. get_unread_summary returns the newest unread message at 2026-07-23T15:12Z = THURSDAY Jul 23, 11:12am EDT — mid-morning local, so UTC and local calendar day agree (no reject flags). search_email is mocked consistently, including a NEWER but already-read message (Greg Chen, Fri Jul 24 12:00pm EDT) as a content distractor: the newest UNREAD is still the Jul 23 helpdesk email. Older unread rows (Tue Jul 21, Mon Jul 20) are decoys for 'most recent'.

Jul 1 00:00 ET = [2026-04-01T04:00Z, 2026-07-01T04:00Z) — nl2time agrees. scenarios.title: omar-last-friday
scenarios.user: Did Omar send me anything last Friday?

checks.note: Only the podcast-draft email is from Omar on Friday Jul 10
Should confirm the Friday podcast email; the Monday reply and the Strava digest don't count

scenarios.rationale: Now = WEDNESDAY Jul 15 2026, 1:05pm EDT. 'Last Friday' from a Wednesday is the most recent past Friday, Jul 10 — and Friday-of-last-week is also Jul 10 under both week conventions, so the phrase is unambiguous: [Jul 10 00:00 ET, Jul 11 00:00 ET) = [2026-07-10T04:00Z, 2026-07-11T04:00Z) — nl2time agrees. Deliberately trap-free (honest baseline): all rows sit mid-day ET so UTC and local days coincide everywhere. In range: Omar's podcast draft (Fri 1:30pm EDT) and the Strava digest (Fri 3:00pm EDT, wrong sender); Omar's Monday Jul 13 reply is outside. Answer: yes — one email.
